candidates.exact_span: The following Minimum Quantification Levels (MQL's) are to be used for reporting pollutant data for NPDES permit applications and/or compliance reporting.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether MQL rules apply to compliance reporting (versus permit-application reporting only) affects whether reported values for listed pollutants support numeric limit comparison (Purpose A) and how below-threshold or non-quantified results are classified versus unresolved missing evidence (Purpose C). The 'and/or' scope is ambiguous as to which reporting contexts are covered.

The stated concentration unit for all tabulated MQL values governs conversion and comparison against reported measurements and enforceable limits; a different unit interpretation would change whether a reported value is above or below the applicable MQL and thus whether numeric compliance comparison is applicable (Purpose A) or how non-quantified results are categorized (Purpose C).

Two distinct MQL values are listed for Mercury with a footnote marker (*1) but no footnote text appears in this segment; different readings of which value applies (or what *1 signifies) would change whether reported mercury results are treated as quantified, below MQL, or lacking adequate evidence for limit comparison (Purpose A) and missing-evidence classification (Purpose C).

Separate MQL entries for total cyanide versus weak-acid-dissociable cyanide require matching the reported parameter to the correct row; misidentifying which cyanide form was measured would change the applicable MQL threshold and thus whether a reported value supports numeric limit comparison (Purpose A) or is classified as below quantification or unresolved (Purpose C).

The pollutant name is misspelled ('Thalllium' versus thallium); different name-matching rules could fail to link reported thallium measurements to this MQL row, leaving the applicable quantification threshold unresolved and changing limit-comparison applicability (Purpose A) and missing-evidence disposition (Purpose C).

The pollutant name is misspelled ('Clorodibromomethane' versus chlorodibromomethane); different name-matching rules could fail to associate reported measurements with this MQL, affecting whether results are treated as quantified for compliance comparison (Purpose A) or left unresolved for missing-evidence analysis (Purpose C).

The MQL of 33 µg/l for total residual chlorine sets the reporting quantification floor for that parameter; whether a reported chlorine result is at or below this level determines if a numeric compliance comparison against a discharge limit can be performed (Purpose A) or if the result must be treated as non-quantified or otherwise documented (Purpose C).

The extremely low dioxin MQL governs whether reported TCDD values are considered quantified; interpretation of results near or below 0.00001 µg/l changes whether numeric limit exceedance can be evaluated (Purpose A) and whether the case is a documented below-quantification state versus inadequate evidence (Purpose C).
